body:
## Summary

Turn the normalized usage records from #180 into a durable audit trail on GitHub: a **ledger** (one record per session per workflow stage, holding per-model breakdowns), a **rendered comment body** (markdown table with a separate row for each model used, above a collapsed JSON block), and an **upsert** that creates or updates a single dedicated audit comment on an issue or PR.

Part 2 of 3, split out of the original combined spec:

- **#180 — probe core + harness adapters** (dependency)
- **#181 (this issue) — ledger, rendering, and the GitHub audit comment**
- **#182 — the shared `agent-usage-audit` skill and wiring the three workflow skills**

**Depends on #180** — this issue consumes the normalized record shape that issue defines.

## Motivation / Context

The probe measures; this makes the measurement durable and readable in the place the work already lives. Both purposes of the original spec ride on this layer: **cost tracking** needs the rows to accumulate across sittings and stages, and **provenance** needs them to survive as an auditable record next to the issue or PR they describe.

## Audit placement

**Dedicated audit comment** — one `🤖 Agent usage` comment per issue or PR, found and updated **by marker content only** (`<!-- BEGIN AGENT USAGE -->` / `<!-- END AGENT USAGE -->`), never by comment position and never `--edit-last`.

Never touches spec bodies or PR descriptions. This keeps the squash-merge commit prefill clean (the PR description doubles as the squash message in this repo's workflow) and poses zero risk to the plan-marker gating that `issue-to-plan` and `plan-to-implementation` depend on — the plan comment is a different comment with different markers.

This choice is validated by prior art: [pr-cost](https://github.com/jabertuhin/pr-cost) embeds cost blocks in PR descriptions, which is exactly the pollution this repo avoids.

## Attribution model

**Per-session ledger rows** — each skill run (per sitting) contributes one record keyed by `(session_id, stage)`: session id, stage, harness, models, model breakdowns, tokens, source. Re-running a stage within one sitting refreshes that record in place; a new sitting adds a record. Multi-sitting flows are therefore counted exactly once each.

**Per-model rows in the summary table** — the PR comment summary markdown table renders a **separate row for each model used**. If a session used multiple models (for instance, if opencode used two different models when using subagent-driven-development: one orchestrator, another for implementing or exploring), the table renders two rows for that opencode session with the tokens divided accordingly. Table columns: `| Stage | Session | Harness | Model | Input | Output | Cache Read | Cache Write | Total | Source |` (with `Model` singular).

**Subagents: rolled up + JSON breakdown** — the table displays each model's divided tokens; the JSON carries the `children` array (session id, model, tokens) for SDD implementer/reviewer provenance.

The ledger is append-and-refresh only: never delete or rewrite another session's record.

## Audit comment format

**Markdown table above, JSON below in a collapsed `<details>` block.** The table is the human-scannable view; the JSON is the append-only machine-readable source of truth, and the table is regenerated from it on every update. A row whose source is `unavailable` renders honestly (em-dashes, `unavailable` source) rather than as zeros, and is excluded from the totals row.

## Requirements

- Ledger merge: exactly one record per `(session_id, stage)`; upsert, never duplicate; stable ordering by workflow stage then timestamp
- Render: markdown table with a separate row for each model used (`stage, session, harness, model, input, output, cache read, cache write, total, source`) plus a totals row, followed by a collapsed `<details>` block holding the ledger JSON in a fenced ```json block
- Multi-model sessions: when `model_breakdowns` contains multiple models (e.g. subagent-driven development using an orchestrator model and an implementation model), render a row for each model with its divided tokens
- Round-trip: the ledger JSON parses back out of a rendered comment body; unparseable or absent JSON yields an empty ledger rather than an error
- Comment lookup by marker content only — never positional, never `--edit-last`, never the plan comment
- Upsert through `gh api` against `repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/comments` (PR conversation comments are issue comments, so one code path serves both `issue:N` and `pr:M` targets)
- A `--dry-run` mode prints the body without posting
- GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit is a hard error to report — never a reason to trim or summarize the ledger
- Never write usage into an issue body, a PR description, or the plan comment
- No local ledger state — the GitHub comment is the ledger

## Non-goals

- No price-list cost computation (pass through reported cost only)
- No aggregation dashboard (the JSON is machine-readable; scripts can come later)
- No changes to issue bodies, PR descriptions, or plan comments
- No harness-specific logic — that all lives in #180's adapters

## Testing

- Ledger tests: append a record, refresh a record in place by `(session_id, stage)`, regenerate the table from JSON, render the `unavailable` path
- Table rendering tests: multi-model session renders separate rows for each model with divided tokens; single-model session renders one row; totals row correctly sums across all model rows; `unavailable` row renders honestly
- Round-trip test: render a ledger, parse it back out of the rendered body
- Posting tests against a stubbed `gh` on `PATH` that records its argv: creates when no audit comment exists, PATCHes the existing one when it does, never selects a plan comment (`<!-- BEGIN PLAN -->`) as the audit comment, `--dry-run` performs no write
- Executable support file → `just test-unit` + `just test` per docs/TESTING.md

## Splitting note

Split out of the original combined issue #180 during `issue-to-plan`: the single plan came to ~86k characters, over GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit used for the planning handoff. Per that workflow the source issue is split rather than the plan compressed. The full brainstorm log lives on #180.
title: feat(skills): agent usage ledger and GitHub audit comment
